transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
States appear to be experiencing higher turnout for the midterms,
according to early voting data,
especially among black voters in the southern U.S.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports that's made several races more competitive.
Across the South, black voters have made up a larger than normal share
of the electorate in early voting.
One reason is the Supreme Court ruling earlier this year
that gutted part of the Voting Rights Act
and led southern Republican-led states
to redraw House maps that minimize black voting power.
That turbocharged turnout could make a difference
in previously long-shot Senate races in South Carolina,
Louisiana, and Mississippi,
Governor's races in Georgia and Florida,
and House races in Tennessee and Alabama,
where GOP gerrymandering could backfire.
It's not just black voters.
Early voting data also shows a surge in younger voters and Latino voters,
as many states report more ballots cast compared to 2022.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Voters in Texas could help decide which party controls the U.S. Senate.
The Texas newsroom's Blaze Ganey spoke with voters
waiting to cast their ballots today.
In Austin, product and graphic designer Maggie Gibson was waiting to vote.
She had a message for anyone considering sitting this election out.
This is a potentially historic election.
I think I've known living in Texas my entire life
that the people of this state deserve better and don't miss out.
It's a really cool and exciting thing to be a part of.
Joe James, a grandfather, believes this election is pivotal for Americans.
I'm 60, and, you know, for me,
this is probably the most important one that I've ever voted in.
More than 7.7 million Texans voted early,
breaking the state's early voting record for a midterm election.
For NPR News, I'm Blaze Ganey in Austin.
To res control of both chambers from the GOP,
Democrats would need a net gain of three seats in the House
and four in the Senate.
Historically, turnout is about 30 percent lower in midterms
compared to presidential elections.
Then again, the University of Florida election lab says
roughly 60 million people already voted before today.
Well, the Department of Justice says
it has sent election monitors to all 50 states.
The DOJ arguing personnel are deployed to ensure election integrity.
Here's NPR's Nate Perez.
For the first time ever,
the Justice Department is sending a thousand monitors
to oversee the midterm elections.
The agency says the efforts are to protect election integrity,
one of the administration's top priorities.
Several election officials have said they're concerned
the election monitors could suppress voter turnout.
The Justice Department has made broad accusations of voter fraud
and filed lawsuits that courts have repeatedly struck down.
The agency has monitored elections for decades,
but it's mostly been to protect the right to vote.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
From Washington, this is NPR.
AI data centers have emerged as a hot-button issue in the midterms.
Voters in at least 40 jurisdictions are deciding
on local ballot measures on whether to allow or restrict them,
weighing the prospect of economic growth against impacts
on surrounding communities.
Australia's highest court has begun hearing a legal challenge
to the government's social media ban for children
brought by the messaging platform Reddit.
As Cristina Coculio reports from Melbourne,
it's the first major legal challenge to the restrictions
nearly a year after they were introduced.
Lawyers for Reddit have urged Australia's high court
to overturn the social media ban they argue was ineptly implemented
and violates the implied freedom of political communication
for children under 16.
To win, they'll have to convince the court that the policy
robs children of a significant form of political expression.
The ban requires some of the world's leading digital platforms
to prevent underage users from holding accounts.
The Australian government has vowed to protect young people
from online harm.
A second challenge by a group known as the Digital Freedom Project
is being jointly heard over a two-day period in Canberra.
Lawyers for both plaintiffs argue if successful,
the case could have significant implications for the ban
and social media platforms.
For NPR News, I'm Cristina Coculio in Melbourne.
The head of Britain's cybersecurity is projecting
artificial intelligence breaches on critical infrastructure
in the UK by 2028.
In a report out today, Richard Horn warns
outdated technology exposes the region to cyber attacks
that could lead to severe disruptions to the public,
such as power outages.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Early voting data shows higher turnout among Black, younger, and Latino voters, boosting several competitive races
Texas voters cast ballots in Austin; more than 7.7 million Texans voted early, a state midterm record
Democrats would need net gains of three House seats and four Senate seats to flip Congress
Justice Department deploys about 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states for the midterms
Voters in at least 40 jurisdictions decide local ballot measures on allowing or restricting AI data centers
Reddit challenges Australia's under-16 social media ban in the country's High Court in Canberra
UK cybersecurity chief Richard Horn warns of AI-driven breaches on critical infrastructure by 2028
